result: CONFIRMED, root-caused to specific code, not a HomeBase-only defect. (1) analyzeImpact() (impact-analysis.ts) is a fixed 15-category, ~90-keyword substring classifier; for the HomeBase description it matched only 2 of 15 categories (screens via the word 'view', costs via 'expense') -- data, permissions, workflows, monetization, actions, and businessLogic all failed to match despite being semantically present, because the classifier requires literal keywords ('record', 'role', 'workflow', 'payment', etc.) the description never happens to use. (2) extractTargetCustomer()'s single regex (/\bfor\s+(.+?)(?:[.!?]|$)/i) found no match, so targetCustomer/targetUsers were empty despite the text being saturated with audience information ('busy families', 'Parents', 'Children'). (3) deriveOpenQuestions() unconditionally asked 'Does this product need more than one user role (e.g. customer vs. owner)?' because the permissions category wasn't keyword-matched -- reproduced verbatim, even though Parent and Child are named, distinct actors with materially different described UI. (4) blueprint-templates.ts maps each matched category to one of a small set of fixed, generic templates -- the 'data' category's dataModel is always the literal {name:'Record',fields:['id','status','createdAt']}, never derived from the actual nouns in the text (chores, grocery lists, expenses, appointments, schedules, rewards all collapse to nothing, or -- since 'data' wasn't even matched here -- to the same generic Record via the D-0045 fallback). (5) hasPermissionsCategory was false, so roles=['customer'] only -- Parent/Child, or even a generic owner role, never reached the Blueprint despite being named explicitly. (6) validateBlueprint() (blueprint-validation.ts) performs pure structural/shape checks (non-empty arrays, valid output targets, well-formed data models, interaction-contract completeness) with zero requirement-to-content correspondence check, so a Blueprint capturing perhaps 5% of the source text's meaning is unconditionally VALID as long as its arrays are non-empty. (7) runQualityGate() (quality-gate.ts) is also purely structural (data-binding present, alt text present, screens reachable, unwired-button detection, 11 checks total) with no semantic-coverage dimension, so it has no way to reject a structurally-valid-but-hollow product -- confirmed live: passed=true, all 11 checks true, for a Blueprint with 1 role, 2 screens, 1 generic data model, 0 workflows, 0 actions, 0 business rules. (8) deriveMonetizationRecommendations() (business-intelligence.ts) always includes 'one-time payment' as a recommendation even when hasMonetization is false, and the Studio page (page.tsx line 280) renders businessModelBrief.revenueModel ('No revenue model was described') directly above the monetizationRecommendations list ('one-time payment') with no label distinguishing a confirmed customer fact from an always-shown default recommendation -- reproducing the founder-observed contradiction exactly. (9) Truth Status for generation.full_stack_web_app reported IMPLEMENTED with rationale 'Blueprint v1 and Build Plan v1 are ready; screens are live at /preview/<screen>' -- technically accurate about what was generated, but readable by a founder as 'HomeBase was implemented' when what was actually generated bears almost no resemblance to HomeBase.
